guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case for UT San Antonio is less about containing Texas completely and more about whether it can score often enough to stay within the market’s margin. Our efficiency numbers give UT San Antonio’s passing game a plausible route against a Texas pass defense that has been less convincing than the overall team profile. That potential resistance is what keeps our view close to the market rather than fully endorsing a Texas runaway.

The concern is obvious: Texas produced 516 yards at 7.0 yards per play in its opener, while Arch Manning threw for 305 yards and four touchdowns. With four starters back on the offensive line, we see more than one-game explosiveness supporting the favorite’s offensive ceiling. Still, the market already demands substantial separation, and our limited disagreement is not enough to justify taking UT San Antonio at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching UT San Antonio’s passing offense against the Texas pass defense. If UT San Antonio can create sustained offense through the air, it has the clearest path to making the margin uncomfortable for Texas.

The challenge is avoiding drive-ending negative plays. Texas recorded at least 40 sacks and 15 interceptions in each of the past two seasons, and it has forced a turnover in 24 consecutive home games. That does not guarantee another disruptive performance, but it explains why the passing matchup offers both the best argument for UT San Antonio and the biggest threat to that argument.

recent_game.fact: Texas opened the 2026 season with a 59-7 home win over Texas State on Sept. 5.
Texas produced 516 total yards and averaged 7.0 yards per play against Texas State.
Texas forced three turnovers—two fumbles and one interception—against Texas State.

opponent_notes.fact: The 2026 game will be the third meeting between Texas and UTSA, and all three meetings have been scheduled in Austin.

quarterback.fact: Senior quarterback Arch Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns in the 2026 opener against Texas State.
Manning is 13-3 as a starter and 9-0 as a starter at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium.
In 13 starts during 2025, Manning completed 248 of 404 passes for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns while adding 399 rushing yards and a team-high 10 rushing touchdowns.
Against UTSA in 2024, Manning accounted for five touchdowns—four passing and one rushing—and produced a 75-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Wingo and a 67-yard touchdown run.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running backs Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers transferred to Texas in spring 2026 from Arizona State and NC State, respectively.
Smothers recorded 72 rushing yards on 10 attempts and added three receptions for 28 yards and a touchdown against Texas State.
Brown had 11 carries for 34 yards and two touchdowns plus one reception for 11 yards in his Texas debut.
Ryan Wingo caught seven passes for 121 yards and one touchdown in the opener; he led Texas in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns in 2025.
Auburn transfer Cam Coleman made his Texas debut with three receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns against Texas State.
Texas returns 2025 offensive-line starters Trevor Goosby, Brandon Baker, Cole Hutson and Connor Robertson.

Texas added offensive linemen Laurence Seymore III, Melvin Siani and Dylan Sikorski through the transfer portal; the listed offensive-line group entered 2026 with 226 combined games played and 114 starts.
Texas added tight end Michael Masunas from Michigan State; he played in all 12 games with eight starts and recorded 19 catches for 232 yards and three touchdowns in 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: EDGE Colin Simmons returned after leading Texas in 2025 with 15.5 tackles for loss, 12 sacks, 15 pressures, three forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.
Simmons recorded one tackle, a half tackle for loss, one quarterback hurry and one fumble recovery against Texas State.
Defensive back Jelani McDonald recorded eight tackles, including seven solo tackles and one tackle for loss, in the opener.
Linebacker Rasheem Biles, a 2026 transfer from Pitt, recorded one interception and one forced fumble in the season opener.

Texas did not punt against Texas State, its first game without a punt since the 2023 game against Kansas.
